key_insight: FACTR 2 introduces NEXT, a data-driven way to estimate external joint torques on low-cost robot arms without dedicated force sensors. With just 10 minutes of free-motion data and about 1 minute of training, it can produce force estimates close to sensor-based systems and improve contact-rich policy learning.
problem_solved: Many commodity robot arms lack affordable force sensors, making force-sensitive manipulation, teleoperation, and contact-rich policy learning difficult or unreliable.
method: Train Neural External Torque Estimation (NEXT) on short free-motion datasets to infer external joint torques.
Use the learned torque estimates as a substitute for dedicated force sensing during interaction and control.
Apply the estimated force feedback to enable teleoperation and improve learning for manipulation policies.
impact: This lowers the cost and setup barrier for force-aware robotics, making advanced manipulation accessible on commodity arms. For practitioners, it offers a fast, practical way to add force feedback and improve learning performance without specialized hardware.

paper_title: FACTR 2: Learning External Force Sensing for Commodity Robot Arms Improves Policy Learning
paper_authors: Steven Oh, Jason Jingzhou Liu, Tony Tao, Philip Han, Kenneth Shaw
